To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the risks of compound Bayes procedures based on a sample of size n converge to the risk of the Bayes procedure based on the true state distribution as n → ∞ with probability 1, uniformly for all distributions on the state space.

for the finite action case, under very mild conditions on the component problems, the risk of the compound procedure which plays Bayes against the maximum likelihood estimate of G converges almost surely to R(G) and the conditional risk converges almost surely, uniformly over the sample space of the component problems, to its expected value, the Bayes risk of the component problems.

for any compound decision problem, the risks of any compound procedure that is a consistent sequence of Bayes procedures based on a consistent sequence of estimators for the empirical distribution function, converge almost surely to the risk R(G), and that the conditional risks converge almost surely to R(G) for each state.

the following question: Under what conditions does the risk of a compound procedure based on estimating G, playing Bayes against this estimate and averaging the results, approach R(G)?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

for compound decision problems with finite state and action spaces and for compound procedures which are not necessarily symmetric, there is a type of almost sure uniform convergence to R(G), and in the special case when the action spaces are finite, a type of almost surely uniform convergence to R (G) of the conditional risk.

for compound procedures which satisfy a certain "weak continuity" condition (Definition 2.2), the conditional risks of each of the component problems converge almost surely and uniformly to the Bayes risk of that problem given the empirical distribution of states.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have extended the previous results to cover the case of infinite state spaces and infinite action spaces, and have weakened the conditions on the procedures to be considered.
we have obtained a number of new results and have extended the results of [6], [7] and [14] in various directions.

we establish convergence of the risks and conditional risks for a large class of compound procedures to the corresponding risks of Bayes procedures, and that the class of procedures for which the results hold is very large.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the results of [6] and [7] are essentially correct for infinite state spaces and infinite action spaces, provided that the component problems are sufficiently "well-behaved".
in order to prove convergence to the risk of the Bayes procedure, it is not necessary to impose the strong conditions previously imposed on compound procedures.
, under the assumptions we make, the Bayes risk can be approximated to within any desired accuracy by the risk of a compound procedure.
